questions.text:
Let the relation R on the set $M=\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 16\}$ be given by
$R=\{(x, y): 4y=5x-3,\ x, y \in M\}$.
Then the minimum number of elements required to be added in R, in order to make the relation symmetric, is equal to
questions.sol:
$4y=5x-3$ needs $5x\equiv3 \pmod 4$, i.e. $x\equiv3 \pmod 4$.
$x=3\Rightarrow y=3$; $x=7\Rightarrow y=8$; $x=11\Rightarrow y=13$; $x=15\Rightarrow y=18\notin M$.
$R=\{(3,3),(7,8),(11,13)\}$. For symmetry add $(8,7)$ and $(13,11)$: $2$ elements.

questions.text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5-x}{3+2x}\right)+\dfrac{1}{\log_e(10-x)}$ is $(-\infty, \alpha] \cup [\beta, \gamma)-\{\delta\}$, then $6(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{5-x}{3+2x}\le1 \iff \dfrac{3x-2}{2x+3}\ge0 \iff x<-\dfrac32$ or $x\ge\dfrac23$.
$\dfrac{5-x}{3+2x}\ge-1 \iff \dfrac{x+8}{2x+3}\ge0 \iff x\le-8$ or $x>-\dfrac32$.
Together: $x\le-8$ or $x\ge\dfrac23$. The log term needs $x<10$ and $10-x\ne1$, i.e. $x\ne9$.
Domain $(-\infty,-8]\cup\left[\dfrac23,10\right)-\{9\}$, so $6\left(-8+\dfrac23+10+9\right)=6\cdot\dfrac{35}{3}=70$.

questions.text: The number of distinct real solutions of the equation $x|x+4|+3|x+2|+10=0$ is
questions.sol:
$x\ge-2$: $x^2+7x+16=0$, discriminant $49-64<0$, no root.
$-4\le x<-2$: $x^2+4x-3x-6+10=x^2+x+4=0$, no real root.
$x<-4$: $-x^2-4x-3x-6+10=0 \Rightarrow x^2+7x-4=0$, $x=\dfrac{-7\pm\sqrt{65}}{2}$; only $\dfrac{-7-\sqrt{65}}{2}\approx-7.53$ is below $-4$.
So there is exactly $1$ solution.

questions.text: Two distinct numbers $a$ and $b$ are selected at random from $1, 2, 3, \ldots, 50$. The probability, that their product $ab$ is divisible by 3, is
questions.sol:
There are $16$ multiples of 3 in $1$ to $50$, and $34$ other numbers.
$P(3\nmid ab)=\dfrac{{}^{34}C_2}{{}^{50}C_2}=\dfrac{561}{1225}$.
So $P(3\mid ab)=1-\dfrac{561}{1225}=\dfrac{664}{1225}$.

questions.text:
If a random variable $x$ has the probability distribution
$x$$0$$1$$2$$3$$4$$5$$6$$7$
$P(x)$$0$$2k$$k$$3k$$2k^2$$2k$$k^2+k$$7k^2$
then $P(3<x\le6)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Total probability: $10k^2+9k=1\Rightarrow(10k-1)(k+1)=0\Rightarrow k=0.1$.
$P(3<x\le6)=P(4)+P(5)+P(6)=2k^2+2k+k^2+k=3k^2+3k=0.03+0.3=0.33$.

questions.text: If the line $\alpha x+2y=1$, where $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, does not meet the hyperbola $x^2-9y^2=9$, then a possible value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.sol:
Put $y=\dfrac{1-\alpha x}{2}$: $4x^2-9(1-\alpha x)^2=36\Rightarrow(4-9\alpha^2)x^2+18\alpha x-45=0$.
No real root needs discriminant $<0$: $324\alpha^2+180(4-9\alpha^2)<0\Rightarrow\alpha^2>\dfrac59$, i.e. $|\alpha|>0.745$ (and $\alpha=\pm\frac23$, where the equation is linear, gives a meeting point).
Of the options only $0.8$ works.

questions.text: Let the set of all values of $r$, for which the circles $(x+1)^2+(y+4)^2=r^2$ and $x^2+y^2-4x-2y-4=0$ intersect at two distinct points be the interval $(\alpha, \beta)$. Then $\alpha\beta$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Centres $(-1,-4)$ and $(2,1)$; radii $r$ and $3$. Distance between centres $=\sqrt{9+25}=\sqrt{34}$.
Two points of intersection: $|r-3|<\sqrt{34}<r+3$, i.e. $\sqrt{34}-3<r<\sqrt{34}+3$.
$\alpha\beta=34-9=25$.

questions.text: The number of solutions of $\tan^{-1}4x+\tan^{-1}6x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, where $-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt6}<x<\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt6}$, is equal to
questions.sol:
In the given range $24x^2<1$, so $\tan^{-1}4x+\tan^{-1}6x=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{10x}{1-24x^2}$.
$\dfrac{10x}{1-24x^2}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\Rightarrow24x^2+10\sqrt3\,x-1=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{-10\sqrt3\pm\sqrt{396}}{48}$.
$x\approx0.054$ lies in the range; $x\approx-0.776$ does not. So $1$ solution.

questions.text: Let $\overrightarrow{AB}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$. Let the projection of the vector $\vec{v}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ on the diagonal $\overrightarrow{AC}$ of the parallelogram ABCD be of length one unit. If $\alpha, \beta$, where $\alpha>\beta$, be the roots of the equation $\lambda^2x^2-6\lambda x+5=0$, then $2\alpha-\beta$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\overrightarrow{AC}=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{AD}=3\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+(\lambda-5)\hat{k}$.
Projection $=\dfrac{3+6+\lambda-5}{\sqrt{45+(\lambda-5)^2}}=1\Rightarrow(\lambda+4)^2=45+(\lambda-5)^2\Rightarrow18\lambda=54\Rightarrow\lambda=3$.
$9x^2-18x+5=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac53,\dfrac13$. So $2\alpha-\beta=\dfrac{10}{3}-\dfrac13=3$.

questions.text: If the image of the point $P(1, 2, a)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-6}{3}=\dfrac{y-7}{2}=\dfrac{7-z}{2}$ is $Q(5, b, c)$, then $a^2+b^2+c^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The line is $(6+3t, 7+2t, 7-2t)$ with direction $(3,2,-2)$.
The midpoint of PQ, $\left(3, \dfrac{2+b}{2}, \dfrac{a+c}{2}\right)$, lies on the line: $6+3t=3\Rightarrow t=-1$, midpoint $(3,5,9)$. So $b=8$, $a+c=18$.
$\overrightarrow{PQ}=(4,6,c-a)\perp(3,2,-2)$: $12+12-2(c-a)=0\Rightarrow c-a=12$. So $a=3$, $c=15$.
$a^2+b^2+c^2=9+64+225=298$.

questions.text: Let $f:[1, \infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function. If $6\displaystyle\int_1^x f(t)\,dt=3xf(x)+x^3-4$ for all $x\ge1$, then the value of $f(2)-f(3)$ is
questions.sol:
At $x=1$: $0=3f(1)-3\Rightarrow f(1)=1$.
Differentiate: $6f=3f+3xf'+3x^2\Rightarrow xf'-f=-x^2\Rightarrow\left(\dfrac{f}{x}\right)'=-1$.
$\dfrac{f}{x}=-x+C$, and $f(1)=1$ gives $C=2$: $f(x)=2x-x^2$.
$f(2)-f(3)=0-(-3)=3$.

questions.text: Let the line $x=-1$ divide the area of the region $\{(x, y): 1+x^2\le y\le 3-x\}$ in the ratio $m:n$, $\gcd(m, n)=1$. Then $m+n$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The curves meet where $x^2+x-2=0$, i.e. $x=-2, 1$. The height of the region is $2-x-x^2$; let $F(x)=2x-\dfrac{x^2}{2}-\dfrac{x^3}{3}$.
$F(-2)=-\dfrac{10}{3}$, $F(-1)=-\dfrac{13}{6}$, $F(1)=\dfrac76$.
Left part $=F(-1)-F(-2)=\dfrac76$; right part $=F(1)-F(-1)=\dfrac{20}{6}$.
Ratio $7:20$, so $m+n=27$.

questions.text: Let the solution curve of the differential equation $x\,dy-y\,dx=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\,dx$, $x>0$, $y(1)=0$, be $y=y(x)$. Then $y(3)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $y=vx$: $v+xv'=v+\sqrt{1+v^2}\Rightarrow\dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1+v^2}}=\dfrac{dx}{x}$.
$\ln\left(v+\sqrt{1+v^2}\right)=\ln x+C$; $y(1)=0$ gives $C=0$, so $v+\sqrt{1+v^2}=x$.
At $x=3$: $\sqrt{1+v^2}=3-v\Rightarrow v=\dfrac43$, so $y(3)=3v=4$.

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\left(\dfrac{1}{[x]+4}\right)dx$, where $[\cdot]$ denotes the greatest integer function, is
questions.sol:

$=\dfrac{7\pi}{20}-\dfrac{7}{60}=\dfrac{7}{60}(3\pi-1)$.

questions.text:
Let $\alpha=\dfrac{-1+i\sqrt3}{2}$ and $\beta=\dfrac{-1-i\sqrt3}{2}$, $i=\sqrt{-1}$. If
$(7-7\alpha+9\beta)^{20}+(9+7\alpha-7\beta)^{20}+(-7+9\alpha+7\beta)^{20}+(14+7\alpha+7\beta)^{20}=m^{10}$,
then $m$ is ________
questions.sol:
$\alpha=\omega$, $\beta=\omega^2$, with $1+\omega+\omega^2=0$ and $\omega^3=1$.
Let $z=7-7\omega+9\omega^2$. Then $\omega z=9+7\omega-7\omega^2$ and $\omega^2z=-7+9\omega+7\omega^2$: these are the first three brackets.
Their sum of 20th powers is $z^{20}(1+\omega^{20}+\omega^{40})=z^{20}(1+\omega^2+\omega)=0$.
The last bracket is $14+7(\omega+\omega^2)=7$. So $m^{10}=7^{20}=49^{10}$ and $m=49$.

questions.text: Let A be a $3\times3$ matrix such that $A+A^T=O$. If $A\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\3\\2\end{bmatrix}$, $A^2\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-3\\19\\-24\end{bmatrix}$ and $\det(\operatorname{adj}(2\operatorname{adj}(A+I)))=(2)^{\alpha}\cdot(3)^{\beta}\cdot(11)^{\gamma}$, $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are non-negative integers, then $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is equal to ________
questions.sol:
Take $A=\begin{bmatrix}0&a&b\\-a&0&c\\-b&-c&0\end{bmatrix}$. Then $A\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\\0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-a\\-a\\c-b\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\3\\2\end{bmatrix}$, so $a=-3$, $c-b=2$.
$A\begin{bmatrix}3\\3\\2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3a+2b\\-3a+2c\\-3b-3c\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-3\\19\\-24\end{bmatrix}$ gives $b=3$, $c=5$.
$\det(A+I)=1+a^2+b^2+c^2=44$.
For $3\times3$: $\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=(\det M)^2$ and $\det(2\operatorname{adj}(A+I))=8\cdot44^2$.
So the value is $64\cdot44^4=2^6\cdot2^8\cdot11^4=2^{14}\cdot11^4$: $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=14+0+4=18$.

questions.text: Let ABC be a triangle. Consider four points $p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4$ on the side AB, five points $p_5, p_6, p_7, p_8, p_9$ on the side BC, and four points $p_{10}, p_{11}, p_{12}, p_{13}$ on the side AC. None of these points is a vertex of the triangle ABC. Then the total number of pentagons, that can be formed by taking all the vertices from the points $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_{13}$, is ________
questions.sol:
Five vertices with no three collinear means at most 2 from each side, so the split (AB, BC, AC) is $(2,2,1)$, $(2,1,2)$ or $(1,2,2)$.
${}^4C_2\,{}^5C_2\,{}^4C_1+{}^4C_2\,{}^5C_1\,{}^4C_2+{}^4C_1\,{}^5C_2\,{}^4C_2=240+180+240=660$.

questions.text: If $\dfrac{\cos^2 48^\circ-\sin^2 12^\circ}{\sin^2 24^\circ-\sin^2 6^\circ}=\dfrac{\alpha+\beta\sqrt5}{2}$, where $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to ________
questions.sol:
$\cos^2A-\sin^2B=\cos(A+B)\cos(A-B)$ and $\sin^2A-\sin^2B=\sin(A+B)\sin(A-B)$.
Numerator $=\cos60^\circ\cos36^\circ$, denominator $=\sin30^\circ\sin18^\circ$.
Ratio $=\dfrac{\cos36^\circ}{\sin18^\circ}=\dfrac{\sqrt5+1}{\sqrt5-1}=\dfrac{(\sqrt5+1)^2}{4}=\dfrac{3+\sqrt5}{2}$.
So $\alpha=3$, $\beta=1$, and $\alpha+\beta=4$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int(\sin x)^{-\frac{11}{2}}(\cos x)^{-\frac52}dx=-\dfrac{p_1}{q_1}(\cot x)^{\frac92}-\dfrac{p_2}{q_2}(\cot x)^{\frac52}-\dfrac{p_3}{q_3}(\cot x)^{\frac12}+\dfrac{p_4}{q_4}(\cot x)^{-\frac32}+C$, where $p_i$ and $q_i$ are positive integers with $\gcd(p_i, q_i)=1$ for $i=1, 2, 3, 4$ and C is the constant of integration, then $\dfrac{15p_1p_2p_3p_4}{q_1q_2q_3q_4}$ is equal to ________
questions.sol:
The integrand is $(\cot x)^{-5/2}\csc^8x=(\cot x)^{-5/2}(1+\cot^2x)^3\csc^2x$. Put $t=\cot x$, $dt=-\csc^2x\,dx$:
$-\displaystyle\int\left(t^{-5/2}+3t^{-1/2}+3t^{3/2}+t^{7/2}\right)dt=\dfrac23t^{-3/2}-6t^{1/2}-\dfrac65t^{5/2}-\dfrac29t^{9/2}+C$.
So $\dfrac{p_1}{q_1}=\dfrac29$, $\dfrac{p_2}{q_2}=\dfrac65$, $\dfrac{p_3}{q_3}=6$, $\dfrac{p_4}{q_4}=\dfrac23$.
$15\cdot\dfrac{2\cdot6\cdot6\cdot2}{9\cdot5\cdot1\cdot3}=15\cdot\dfrac{144}{135}=16$.

C. Boltzmann constantIII. $ML^2T^{-3}A^{-2}$

questions.text: A meter bridge with two resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ as shown in figure was balanced (null point) at 40 cm from the point $P$. The null point changed to 50 cm from the point $P$, when 16 $\Omega$ resistance is connected in parallel to $R_2$. The values of resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ are ______.
questions.sol:
First balance: $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}=\dfrac{40}{60}=\dfrac23$.
With $16\ \Omega$ in parallel with $R_2$, balance at the middle: $R_1=\dfrac{16R_2}{16+R_2}$.
So $\dfrac23=\dfrac{16}{16+R_2}\Rightarrow R_2=8\ \Omega$ and $R_1=\dfrac{16}{3}\ \Omega$.

questions.text: The escape velocity from a spherical planet $A$ is 10 km/s. The escape velocity from another planet $B$ whose density and radius are 10% of those of planet $A$, is ______ m/s.
questions.sol:
$v_e=\sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}=R\sqrt{\dfrac{8\pi G\rho}{3}}$, so $v_e\propto R\sqrt{\rho}$.
$v_B=10\ \text{km/s}\times0.1\times\sqrt{0.1}=\dfrac{10^4}{10\sqrt{10}}\ \text{m/s}=100\sqrt{10}$ m/s.

questions.text: A projectile is thrown upward at an angle $60^\circ$ with the horizontal. The speed of the projectile is 20 m/s when its direction of motion is $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. The initial speed of the projectile is _______ m/s.
questions.sol:
The horizontal component of velocity does not change: $u\cos60^\circ=20\cos45^\circ$.
$\dfrac{u}{2}=10\sqrt2\Rightarrow u=20\sqrt2$ m/s.

questions.text: Net gravitational force at the center of a square is found to be $F_1$ when four particles having mass $M$, $2M$, $3M$ and $4M$ are placed at the four corners of the square as shown in figure and it is $F_2$ when the positions of $3M$ and $4M$ are interchanged. The ratio $\dfrac{F_1}{F_2}$ is $\dfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt5}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______.
questions.sol:
Each mass pulls the centre towards its corner with a force proportional to its mass. Put $4M$ at $(-1,1)$, $3M$ at $(1,1)$, $M$ at $(-1,-1)$, $2M$ at $(1,-1)$.
$F_1\propto(-4+3-1+2,\ 4+3-1-2)=(0,4)$, magnitude $4$.
After swapping $3M$ and $4M$: $(-3+4-1+2,\ 3+4-1-2)=(2,4)$, magnitude $2\sqrt5$.
$\dfrac{F_1}{F_2}=\dfrac{4}{2\sqrt5}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt5}$, so $\alpha=2$.

questions.text: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 10 cm is kept in contact with another solid sphere of mass 10 kg and radius 20 cm. The moment of inertia of this pair of spheres about the tangent passing through the point of contact is __________ kg.m$^2$.
questions.sol:
For a solid sphere about a tangent: $I=\dfrac25MR^2+MR^2=\dfrac75MR^2$.
$I=\dfrac75(5)(0.1)^2+\dfrac75(10)(0.2)^2=0.07+0.56=0.63$ kg m$^2$.

questions.text: Rods $x$ and $y$ of equal dimensions but of different materials are joined as shown in figure. Temperatures of end points $A$ and $F$ are maintained at 100 °C and 40 °C respectively. Given the thermal conductivity of rod $x$ is three times of that of rod $y$, the temperature at junction points $B$ and $E$ are (close to):
questions.sol:
Let the thermal resistance of one rod $x$ be $r$; then a rod $y$ has $3r$.
B to E: path BCE $=6r$ in parallel with path BDE $=2r$, giving $\dfrac{6r\cdot2r}{8r}=1.5r$.
Total A to F: $r+1.5r+3r=5.5r$, so the heat current is $\dfrac{60}{5.5r}$.
$T_B=100-\dfrac{60}{5.5}\approx89$ °C; $T_E=40+3\cdot\dfrac{60}{5.5}\approx73$ °C.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Pressure of a fluid is exerted only on a solid surface in contact as the fluid-pressure does not exist everywhere in a still fluid.
Statement II: Excess potential energy of the molecules on the surface of a liquid, when compared to interior, results in surface tension.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is false: pressure exists at every point of a fluid at rest, not only at a solid surface.
Statement II is true: surface molecules have extra potential energy compared with those inside, and this surface energy shows up as surface tension.

questions.text:
A cylindrical tube $AB$ of length $l$, closed at both ends contains an ideal gas of 1 mol having molecular weight $M$. The tube is rotated in a horizontal plane with constant angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis perpendicular to $AB$ and passing through the edge at end $A$, as shown in the figure. If $P_A$ and $P_B$ are the pressures at $A$ and $B$ respectively, then
(Consider the temperature is same at all points in the tube)
questions.sol:
For a gas layer at distance $r$ from the axis: $\dfrac{dP}{dr}=\rho\omega^2r$ with $\rho=\dfrac{PM}{RT}$.
$\dfrac{dP}{P}=\dfrac{M\omega^2}{RT}r\,dr\Rightarrow\ln\dfrac{P_B}{P_A}=\dfrac{M\omega^2l^2}{2RT}$.
So $P_B=P_A\exp\left(\dfrac{M\omega^2l^2}{2RT}\right)$.

questions.text: The volume of an ideal gas increases 8 times and temperature becomes $(1/4)^{\text{th}}$ of initial temperature during a reversible change. If there is no exchange of heat in this process $(\Delta Q=0)$ then identify the gas from the following options (Assuming the gases given in the options are ideal gases):
questions.sol:
Reversible adiabatic: $TV^{\gamma-1}$ is constant, so $\dfrac14\cdot8^{\gamma-1}=1$.
$8^{\gamma-1}=4\Rightarrow3(\gamma-1)=2\Rightarrow\gamma=\dfrac53$: a monatomic gas, He.

questions.text: $XPQY$ is a vertical smooth long loop having a total resistance $R$ where $PX$ is parallel to $QY$ and separation between them is $l$. A constant magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to the plane of the loop exists in the entire space. A rod $CD$ of length $L\ (L>l)$ and mass $m$ is made to slide down from rest under the gravity as shown in figure. The terminal speed acquired by the rod is __________ m/s. ($g$ = acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
Only the length $l$ between the rails is in the circuit. EMF $=Blv$, current $I=\dfrac{Blv}{R}$, magnetic force $=BIl=\dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R}$.
At terminal speed this balances the weight: $\dfrac{B^2l^2v}{R}=mg\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{mgR}{B^2l^2}$.

questions.text:
Six point charges are kept $60^\circ$ apart from each other on the circumference of a circle of radius $R$ as shown in figure. The net electric field at the center of the circle is _______.
($\epsilon_0$ is permittivity of free space)
questions.sol:
Six equal charges $+Q$ would give zero field. The actual set is that, plus a charge $-2Q$ at the position of $-Q$, at $150^\circ$ from the $x$-axis.
A negative charge pulls the field towards itself: $\vec{E}=\dfrac{2Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0R^2}\left(\cos150^\circ\,\hat{i}+\sin150^\circ\,\hat{j}\right)=\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0R^2}\left(-\sqrt3\hat{i}+\hat{j}\right)$.
$=-\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0R^2}\left(\sqrt3\hat{i}-\hat{j}\right)$.

questions.text:
A simple pendulum has a bob with mass $m$ and charge $q$. The pendulum string has negligible mass. When a uniform and horizontal electric field $\vec{E}$ is applied, the tension in the string changes. The final tension in the string, when pendulum attains an equilibrium position is __________.
(g: acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
At equilibrium the tension balances the resultant of the weight $mg$ (vertical) and the electric force $qE$ (horizontal).
$T=\sqrt{(mg)^2+(qE)^2}$.

questions.text: Electric field in a region is given by $\vec{E}=Ax\hat{i}+By\hat{j}$, where $A=10$ V/m$^2$ and $B=5$ V/m$^2$. If the electric potential at a point $(10, 20)$ is 500 V, then the electric potential at origin is________V.

questions.text: Three identical coils $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$ are closely placed such that they share a common axis. $C_2$ is exactly midway. $C_1$ carries current $I$ in anti-clockwise direction while $C_3$ carries current $I$ in clockwise direction. An induced current flows through $C_2$ will be in clockwise direction when
options: $C_1$ and $C_3$ move with equal speeds towards $C_2$
$C_1$ and $C_3$ move with equal speeds away from $C_2$
$C_1$ moves towards $C_2$ and $C_3$ moves away from $C_2$
$C_1$ moves away from $C_2$ and $C_3$ moves towards $C_2$
questions.sol:
The opposite currents in $C_1$ and $C_3$ give opposite fields at $C_2$. Seen from the same side, $C_1$'s anticlockwise current makes a field pointing towards the viewer through $C_2$.
If both coils move symmetrically, the two fields at $C_2$ still cancel, so no current is induced.
If $C_1$ approaches and $C_3$ recedes, the flux towards the viewer grows. By Lenz's law, $C_2$ opposes this with a field away from the viewer, i.e. a clockwise current.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A thin convex lens of focal length 5 cm and a thin concave lens of focal length 4 cm are combined together (without any gap) and this combination has magnification $m_1$ when an object is placed 10 cm before the convex lens. Keeping the positions of convex lens and object undisturbed a gap of 1 cm is introduced between the lenses by moving the concave lens away, which lead to a change in magnification of total lens system to $m_2$. The value of $\left|\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}\right|$ is _________.
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. Working gives |m1/m2| = 5/6, which is not among the options.
questions.sol:
In contact: $\dfrac1F=\dfrac15-\dfrac14=-\dfrac1{20}$. With $u=-10$: $\dfrac1v=-\dfrac1{20}-\dfrac1{10}\Rightarrow v=-\dfrac{20}{3}$, so $m_1=\dfrac{v}{u}=\dfrac23$.
With a 1 cm gap: the convex lens alone gives $\dfrac1v=\dfrac15-\dfrac1{10}\Rightarrow v=10$ cm, magnification $-1$.
This image is a virtual object $9$ cm beyond the concave lens: $\dfrac1v=-\dfrac14+\dfrac19\Rightarrow v=-\dfrac{36}{5}$, magnification $\dfrac{-36/5}{9}=-0.8$.
$m_2=(-1)(-0.8)=0.8$, so $\left|\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}\right|=\dfrac{2/3}{0.8}=\dfrac56$, which is not among the options.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider an equilateral prism (refractive index $\sqrt2$). A ray of light is incident on its one surface at a certain angle $i$. If the emergent ray is found to graze along the other surface then the angle of refraction at the incident surface is close to _______.
questions.sol:
Grazing emergence means the angle inside at the second face is the critical angle: $\sin C=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, $C=45^\circ$.
$r_1+r_2=A=60^\circ\Rightarrow r_1=60^\circ-45^\circ=15^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
7.9 MeV $\alpha$-particle scatters from a target material of atomic number 79. From the given data the estimated diameter of nuclei of the target material is (approximately) ______m.
$\left[\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}=9\times10^9\ \text{Nm}^2/\text{C}^2\text{ and electron charge}=1.6\times10^{-19}\ \text{C}\right]$
questions.sol:
Distance of closest approach (head-on): $r_0=\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\cdot\dfrac{2Ze^2}{K}=\dfrac{9\times10^9\times2\times79\times(1.6\times10^{-19})^2}{7.9\times10^6\times1.6\times10^{-19}}=2.88\times10^{-14}$ m.
Taking this as the estimate of the nuclear radius, the diameter is about $2r_0=5.76\times10^{-14}$ m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The minimum frequency of photon required to break a particle of mass 15.348 amu into 4 $\alpha$ particles is ________ kHz.
[mass of He nucleus = 4.002 amu, 1 amu = $1.66\times10^{-27}$ kg, h = $6.6\times10^{-34}$ J.s and c = $3\times10^8$ m/s]
questions.sol:
Mass to be supplied: $\Delta m=4(4.002)-15.348=0.660$ amu.
$E=\Delta m\,c^2=0.66\times1.66\times10^{-27}\times9\times10^{16}\approx9.86\times10^{-11}$ J.
$\nu=\dfrac{E}{h}=\dfrac{9.86\times10^{-11}}{6.6\times10^{-34}}\approx1.494\times10^{23}$ Hz $=14.94\times10^{19}$ kHz.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Find the correct combination of A, B, C and D inputs which can cause the LED to glow.
questions.sol:
Each of A and B feeds both inputs of a NOR gate, giving $\bar{A}$ and $\bar{B}$. The NAND gate then gives $\overline{\bar{A}\,\bar{B}}=A+B$.
C and D go to a NOR gate: $\overline{C+D}$.
The LED conducts from the NAND output to the NOR output, so it glows when $A+B=1$ and $\overline{C+D}=0$, i.e. at least one of A, B and at least one of C, D is 1.
Only 1101 satisfies both.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A circular disc has radius $R_1$ and thickness $T_1$. Another circular disc made of the same material has radius $R_2$ and thickness $T_2$. If the moment of inertia of both discs are same and $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}=2$ then $\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}=\dfrac{1}{\alpha}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _________.
questions.sol:
$I=\dfrac12MR^2$ with $M=\rho\pi R^2T$, so $I\propto R^4T$.
$R_1^4T_1=R_2^4T_2\Rightarrow\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}=\left(\dfrac{R_2}{R_1}\right)^4=\dfrac{1}{16}$, so $\alpha=16$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text:
Two loudspeakers ($L_1$ and $L_2$) are placed with a separation of 10 m, as shown in figure. Both speakers are fed with an audio input signal of same frequency with constant volume. A voice recorder, initially at point $A$, at equidistance to both loud speakers, is moved by 25 m along the line $AB$ while monitoring the audio signal. The measured signal was found to undergo 10 cycles of minima and maxima during the movement. The frequency of the input signal is ______Hz
(Speed of sound in air is 324 m/s and $\sqrt5=2.23$)
questions.sol:
Take the speakers at $(0,\pm5)$ m and AB along $x=40$ m, from $y=0$ to $y=25$ m.
At A the path difference is $0$. At B: $\sqrt{40^2+30^2}-\sqrt{40^2+20^2}=50-20\sqrt5=50-44.6=5.4$ m.
10 cycles of maxima and minima means the path difference changed by $10\lambda$: $\lambda=0.54$ m.
$f=\dfrac{324}{0.54}=600$ Hz.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Inductance of a coil with $10^4$ turns is 10 mH and it is connected to a dc source of 10 V with internal resistance of 10 $\Omega$. The energy density in the inductor when the current reaches $\left(\dfrac1e\right)$ of its maximum value is $\alpha\pi\times\dfrac{1}{e^2}$ J/m$^3$. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
($\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ Tm/A).
questions.sol:
Maximum current $=\dfrac{10}{10}=1$ A, so $I=\dfrac1e$ A.
The length of the coil is not given; the intended working takes the $10^4$ turns as $n=10^4$ turns per metre, so $B=\mu_0nI$.
$u=\dfrac{B^2}{2\mu_0}=\dfrac{\mu_0n^2I^2}{2}=\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times10^8}{2e^2}=\dfrac{20\pi}{e^2}$ J/m$^3$, so $\alpha=20$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave, travelling in an unknown non-magnetic medium is given by,
$E_y=20\sin(3\times10^6x-4.5\times10^{14}t)$ V/m
(where $x$, t and other values have S.I. units). The dielectric constant of the medium is __________
(speed of light in free space is $3\times10^8$ m/s)
questions.sol:
Speed in the medium $v=\dfrac{\omega}{k}=\dfrac{4.5\times10^{14}}{3\times10^6}=1.5\times10^8$ m/s.
Refractive index $n=\dfrac{c}{v}=2$; for a non-magnetic medium the dielectric constant is $n^2=4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel beam of light travelling in air (refractive index 1.0) is incident on a convex spherical glass surface of radius of curvature 50 cm. Refractive index of glass is 1.5. The rays converge to a point at a distance $x$ cm from the centre of the curvature of the spherical surface. The value of $x$ is ________ cm.
questions.sol:
Refraction at one surface: $\dfrac{\mu_2}{v}-\dfrac{\mu_1}{u}=\dfrac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R}$ with $u=\infty$: $\dfrac{1.5}{v}=\dfrac{0.5}{50}\Rightarrow v=150$ cm from the pole.
The centre of curvature is 50 cm from the pole, so $x=150-50=100$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
In the reaction,
$\mathrm{2Al(s)+6HCl(aq)\longrightarrow2Al^{3+}(aq)+6Cl^-(aq)+3H_2(g)}$
options: 12 L HCl(aq) is consumed for every 6L $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$ produced.
33.6 L $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$ is produced regardless of temperature and pressure for every mole of Al that reacts.
67.2 L $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$ at STP is produced for every mole of Al that reacts.
11.2 L $\mathrm{H_2(g)}$ at STP is produced for every mole of HCl consumed.
questions.sol:
6 mol HCl give 3 mol $\mathrm{H_2}$, so 1 mol HCl gives 0.5 mol $\mathrm{H_2}=11.2$ L at STP. True.
1 mol Al gives 1.5 mol $\mathrm{H_2}=33.6$ L only at STP (not regardless of conditions), not 67.2 L.
HCl is in solution, so a gas-volume ratio does not apply to it.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The energy required by electrons, present in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom to be excited to second Bohr orbit is ____________J mol$^{-1}$.
Given: $R_H=2.18\times10^{-11}$ ergs.
questions.sol:
$R_H=2.18\times10^{-11}$ erg $=2.18\times10^{-18}$ J.
Per atom: $\Delta E=R_H\left(1-\dfrac14\right)=1.635\times10^{-18}$ J.
Per mole: $1.635\times10^{-18}\times6.02\times10^{23}\approx9.8\times10^5$ J mol$^{-1}$, the option $9.835\times10^5$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The formal charges on the atoms marked as (1) to (4) in the Lewis representation of $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ molecule respectively are
questions.sol:
Formal charge $=$ valence electrons $-$ non-bonding electrons $-\dfrac12$(bonding electrons).
(1) O bonded to H and N, two lone pairs: $6-4-2=0$.
(2) N with four bonds, no lone pair: $5-0-4=+1$.
(3) Double-bonded O, two lone pairs: $6-4-2=0$.
(4) Single-bonded O, three lone pairs: $6-6-1=-1$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I
Thermodynamic Process		List-II
Magnitude in kJ
A. Work done in reversible, isothermal expansion of 2 mol of ideal gas from 2 dm$^3$ to 20 dm$^3$ at 300 K.I. 4
B. Work done in irreversible isothermal expansion of 1 mol ideal gas from 1 m$^3$ to 3 m$^3$ at 300 K against a constant pressure of 3kPa.II. 11.5
C. Change in internal energy for adiabatic expansion of a 1 mol ideal gas with change of temperature = 320 K and $\bar{C}_V=\dfrac32R$.III. 6
D. Change in enthalpy at constant pressure of 1 mol ideal gas with change of temperature = 337 K and $\bar{C}_p=\dfrac52R$.IV. 7
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: $nRT\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}=2\times8.314\times300\times2.303\approx11.5$ kJ (II).
B: $p\Delta V=3\ \text{kPa}\times2\ \text{m}^3=6$ kJ (III).
C: $\Delta U=\dfrac32R\Delta T=1.5\times8.314\times320\approx4.0$ kJ (I).
D: $\Delta H=\dfrac52R\Delta T=2.5\times8.314\times337\approx7.0$ kJ (IV).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The Henry's law constant $K_H$ is constant with respect to variations in solution's concentration over the range for which the solution is ideally dilute.
Statement II: $K_H$ does not differ for the same solute in different solvents.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is true: in the ideally dilute range $p=K_Hx$ with $K_H$ independent of concentration (it depends on temperature and the nature of the gas and solvent).
Statement II is false: $K_H$ depends on the solvent as well as the solute.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider a solution of $\mathrm{CO_2(g)}$ dissolved in water in a closed container.
Which one of the following plots correctly represents variation of log (partial pressure of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ in vapour phase above water) [$y$-axis] with log (mole fraction of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ in water) [$x$-axis] at 25°C?
questions.sol:
Henry's law: $p=K_Hx$, so $\log p=\log x+\log K_H$.
The plot is a straight line of slope 1 with intercept $\log K_H$. For $\mathrm{CO_2}$ at 25 °C, $K_H\approx1.67\times10^8$ Pa, so the intercept is positive and the line does not pass through the origin: the third graph.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A 'p'-block element (E) and hydrogen form a binary cation $(\mathrm{EH_x})^+$, while $\mathrm{EH_3}$ on treatment with $\mathrm{K_2HgI_4}$ in alkaline medium gives a precipitate of basic mercury(II)amido-iodine. Given below are first ionisation enthalpy values (kJ mol$^{-1}$) for first element each from group 13, 14, 15 and 16. Identify the correct first ionisation enthalpy value for element E.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{EH_3}$ giving a brown precipitate with Nessler's reagent (alkaline $\mathrm{K_2HgI_4}$) is ammonia, and $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ is the cation, so E is nitrogen.
The listed values belong to B (801), C (1086), N (1402) and O (given as 1312; about 1314) kJ mol$^{-1}$; nitrogen's half-filled 2p subshell gives it a higher value than oxygen.
So E has 1402 kJ mol$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
A $\rightarrow$ product (First order reaction).
Three sets of experiment were performed for a reaction under similar experimental conditions:
Run 1 $\Rightarrow$ 100 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A
Run 2 $\Rightarrow$ 200 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A
Run 3 $\Rightarrow$ 100 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A + 100 mL of $\mathrm{H_2O}$ added.
The correct variation of rate of reaction is
questions.sol:
For a first-order reaction, rate $=k[\mathrm{A}]$ depends on concentration, not on the volume taken.
Runs 1 and 2 are both 10 M, so equal rates. Run 3 is diluted to 5 M, so its rate is half.
Run 3 < Run 1 = Run 2.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Two p-block elements X and Y form fluorides of the type $\mathrm{EF_3}$. The fluoride compound $\mathrm{XF_3}$ is a Lewis acid and $\mathrm{YF_3}$ is a Lewis base. The hybridizations of the central atoms of $\mathrm{XF_3}$ and $\mathrm{YF_3}$ respectively are
questions.sol:
An electron-deficient $\mathrm{EF_3}$ such as $\mathrm{BF_3}$ is a Lewis acid: three bond pairs, no lone pair, $sp^2$.
An $\mathrm{EF_3}$ with a lone pair such as $\mathrm{NF_3}$ can act as a Lewis base: three bond pairs and one lone pair, $sp^3$.
So $sp^2$ and $sp^3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The halogen that makes longest bond with hydrogen in HX, has the smallest covalent radius in its group.
Statement II: A group 15 element's hydride $\mathrm{EH_3}$ has the lowest boiling point among corresponding hydrides of other group 15 elements. The maximum covalency of that element E is 4.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: the longest H-X bond is in HI, and iodine has the largest covalent radius in group 17. False.
Statement II: the group 15 hydride with the lowest boiling point is $\mathrm{PH_3}$ ($\mathrm{NH_3}$ is raised by hydrogen bonding). Phosphorus can use d orbitals and show covalency above 4 (e.g. 5 in $\mathrm{PCl_5}$, 6 in $\mathrm{PCl_6^-}$). False.
Both statements are false.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: A first row transition metal (M) does not liberate $\mathrm{H_2}$ gas from dilute HCl. 1 mol of aqueous solution of $\mathrm{MSO_4}$ is treated with excess of aqueous KCN and then $\mathrm{H_2S(g)}$ is passed through the solution. The amount of MS (metal sulphide) formed from the above reaction is __________ mol.
questions.sol:
Copper is the first-row transition metal with a positive $E^\circ(\mathrm{M^{2+}/M})$, so it does not liberate $\mathrm{H_2}$ from dilute HCl.
With excess KCN, $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ is reduced and complexed as the very stable $\mathrm{[Cu(CN)_4]^{3-}}$.
The free copper ion concentration is then too low for CuS to precipitate when $\mathrm{H_2S}$ is passed: $0$ mol.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the transition metal ions $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ and all form low spin octahedral complexes. The correct decreasing order of unpaired electrons in their respective d-orbitals of the complexes is
questions.sol:
Low spin octahedral (fill $t_{2g}$ first):
$\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ $d^3$: $t_{2g}^3$, 3 unpaired. $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ $d^4$: $t_{2g}^4$, 2. $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ $d^5$: $t_{2g}^5$, 1. $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ $d^6$: $t_{2g}^6$, 0.
Order: $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}>Mn^{3+}>Fe^{3+}>Co^{3+}}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Phenol on treatment with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$/aq. KOH under refluxing condition, followed by acidification produces $p$-hydroxy benzaldehyde as the major product and $o$-hydroxy benzaldehyde as the minor product.
Statement II: The mixture of $p$-hydroxybenzaldehyde and $o$-hydroxybenzaldehyde can be easily separated through steam distillation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: in the Reimer-Tiemann reaction the major product is $o$-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde), not the para isomer. False.
Statement II: the ortho isomer has intramolecular hydrogen bonding and is steam volatile; the para isomer is held by intermolecular hydrogen bonds and is not. So steam distillation separates them. True.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The correct order of reactivity of $\mathrm{CH_3Br}$ in methanol with the following nucleophiles is
$\mathrm{F^-, I^-, C_2H_5O^-}$ and $\mathrm{C_6H_5O^-}$
questions.sol:
In a protic solvent such as methanol, small anions are strongly solvated, so $\mathrm{F^-}$ is the weakest nucleophile and the large, polarisable $\mathrm{I^-}$ the strongest.
Ethoxide is a stronger nucleophile than phenoxide, whose charge is delocalised into the ring.
Order: $\mathrm{I^->C_2H_5O^->C_6H_5O^->F^-}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Benzene is nitrated to give nitrobenzene, which on further treatment with $\mathrm{CH_3COCl/AlCl_3}$ will give the compound shown in the figure.
Statement II: $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ group is a $m$-directing, and deactivating group.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Statement I: nitrobenzene is so strongly deactivated that it does not undergo Friedel-Crafts acylation (it is even used as a solvent for the reaction). Incorrect.
Statement II: $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ withdraws electrons by $-I$ and $-R$ effects, deactivating the ring and directing to the meta position. Correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The correct order of the rate of reaction of the following reactants with nucleophile by $S_N1$ mechanism is :
(Given : Structures I and II are rigid)
questions.sol:
$S_N1$ rate follows carbocation stability.
I and II are rigid bridgehead bromides: the bridgehead cation cannot become planar, so both react very slowly. The more strained bicyclo[2.2.1] cation (II) is even less stable than the bicyclo[2.2.2] cation (I).
III gives the tertiary butyl cation, and IV the triphenylmethyl cation, which is strongly resonance-stabilised.
Order: II < I < III < IV.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
As compared with chlorocyclohexane, which of the following statements correctly apply to chlorobenzene?
A. The magnitude of negative charge is more on chlorine atom.
B. The C $-$ Cl bond has partial double bond character.
C. C $-$ Cl bond is less polar.
D. C $-$ Cl bond is longer due to repulsion between delocalised electrons of the aromatic ring and lone pairs of electrons of chlorine.
E. The C $-$ Cl bond is formed using $sp^2$ hybridised orbital of carbon.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
In chlorobenzene a lone pair of Cl is delocalised into the ring, giving the C-Cl bond partial double-bond character (B true). The bond is therefore shorter, not longer (D false).
The carbon is $sp^2$ (E true); being more electronegative than $sp^3$ carbon, it makes the bond less polar (C true) and leaves less negative charge on Cl (A false).
Correct: B, C and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I
Reagents		List-II
Name of Reaction involving carbonyl compounds
A. $\mathrm{NH_2-NH_2}$, KOHI. Tollen's Test
B. $\mathrm{Ag(NH_3)_2OH}$II. Clemmensen Reduction
C. Aq. $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$, Sodium Potassium tartarate, KOHIII. Wolff - Kishner Reduction
D. Zn - Hg, HClIV. Fehling's Test
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Hydrazine with KOH (then heating in glycol): Wolff-Kishner reduction (A-III).
Ammoniacal silver nitrate: Tollens' test (B-I).
Copper sulphate with Rochelle salt (sodium potassium tartrate) and alkali: Fehling's test (C-IV).
Zinc amalgam and HCl: Clemmensen reduction (D-II).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: 'A' is a neutral organic compound (M. F : $\mathrm{C_8H_9ON}$). On treatment with aqueous $\mathrm{Br_2/HO^{(-)}}$, 'A' forms a compound 'B' which is soluble in dilute acid. 'B' on treatment with aqueous $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ / HCl (0-5 °C) produces a compound 'C' which on treatment with CuCN/NaCN produces 'D'. Hydrolysis of 'D' produces 'E' which is also obtainable from the hydrolysis of 'A'. 'E' on treatment with acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ produces 'F'. 'F' contains two different types of hydrogen atoms. The structure of 'A' is
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Br_2}$/alkali (Hofmann bromamide) turns a primary amide $\mathrm{ArCONH_2}$ into the amine $\mathrm{ArNH_2}$ (B, soluble in acid). Diazotisation (C) and the Sandmeyer reaction give the nitrile ArCN (D), whose hydrolysis gives ArCOOH (E), the same acid that hydrolysis of the amide A gives. So A is a methylbenzamide, $\mathrm{CH_3C_6H_4CONH_2}$.
$\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ oxidises the methyl group: F is a benzenedicarboxylic acid.
Only terephthalic acid (para) has just two kinds of H (four equivalent ring H and the COOH H). So A is 4-methylbenzamide, the second structure.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Sucrose is dextrorotatory. However, sucrose upon hydrolysis gives a solution having mixture of products. This solution shows laevorotation.
Statement II: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives glucose and fructose. Since the laevorotation of glucose is more than the dextrorotation of fructose, the resulting solution becomes laevorotatory.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is true: sucrose ($+66.5^\circ$) hydrolyses to invert sugar, which is laevorotatory.
Statement II has the roles reversed: glucose is dextrorotatory ($+52.5^\circ$) and fructose laevorotatory ($-92.4^\circ$); the laevorotation of fructose is the larger. False.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Dissociation of a gas $\mathrm{A_2}$ takes place according to the following chemical reaction. At equilibrium, the total pressure is 1 bar at 300K.
$\mathrm{A_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2A(g)}$
The standard Gibbs energy of formation of the involved substances has been provided below:
Substance$\Delta G_f^\circ$/ kJ mol$^{-1}$
$\mathrm{A_2}$$-100.00$
A$-50.832$
The degree of dissociation of $\mathrm{A_2(g)}$ is given by $(x\times10^{-2})^{1/2}$ where $x$ = ___________. (Nearest integer).
[Given: R = 8 J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$, log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.48]
Assume degree of dissociation is not negligible.
questions.sol:
$\Delta G^\circ=2(-50.832)-(-100.00)=-1.664$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
$\ln K=\dfrac{1664}{8\times300}=0.693\Rightarrow K_p=2$.
With degree of dissociation $\alpha$ at total pressure 1 bar: $K_p=\dfrac{4\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2}=2\Rightarrow\alpha^2=\dfrac13$.
$\alpha=(33.3\times10^{-2})^{1/2}$, so $x=33$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following electrochemical cell at 298K
$\mathrm{Pt\,|\,HSnO_2^-(aq)\,|\,Sn(OH)_6^{2-}(aq)\,|\,OH^-(aq)\,|\,Bi_2O_3(s)\,|\,Bi(s)}$.
If the reaction quotient at a given time is $10^6$, then the cell EMF ($E_{\text{cell}}$) is __________ $\times10^{-1}$ V (Nearest integer).
Given the standard half-cell reduction potential as
$E^\circ_{\mathrm{Bi_2O_3/Bi,OH^-}}=-0.44$ V and $E^\circ_{\mathrm{Sn(OH)_6^{2-}/HSnO_2^-,OH^-}}=-0.90$ V
questions.sol:
Anode: $\mathrm{HSnO_2^-}\to\mathrm{Sn(OH)_6^{2-}}$ (Sn(II) to Sn(IV), 2 e$^-$). Cathode: $\mathrm{Bi_2O_3}\to2\mathrm{Bi}$ (6 e$^-$). Balanced overall: $n=6$.
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=-0.44-(-0.90)=0.46$ V.
$E=0.46-\dfrac{0.0591}{6}\log10^6=0.46-0.059\approx0.40$ V $=4\times10^{-1}$ V.

questions.text:
The cycloalkene (X) on bromination consumes one mole of bromine per mole of (X) and gives the product (Y) in which C:Br ratio is 3:1. The percentage of bromine in the product (Y) is ___________%. (Nearest integer)
(Given : molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, O : 16, Br : 80)
questions.sol:
A cycloalkene with one double bond is $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}}$; adding one $\mathrm{Br_2}$ gives $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}Br_2}$.
C:Br $=3:1$ gives $n=6$: Y is $\mathrm{C_6H_{10}Br_2}$, $M=72+10+160=242$.
%Br $=\dfrac{160}{242}\times100\approx66.1$, i.e. $66$.

questions.text:
Sodium fusion extract of an organic compound (Y) with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and chlorine water gives violet color to the $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ layer. 0.15g of (Y) gave 0.12 g of the silver halide precipitate in Carius method. Percentage of halogen in the compound (Y) is __________. (Nearest integer)
(Given : molar mass g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, Cl : 35.5, Br : 80, I : 127)
questions.sol:
A violet chloroform layer shows iodine, so the precipitate is AgI ($M=108+127=235$).
%I $=\dfrac{127}{235}\times\dfrac{0.12}{0.15}\times100\approx43.2$, i.e. $43$.
